objection: Weak objection: the strongest case is that his lead is partly unreviewed volume. About 32% of his 2,939 PRs are templated add-source/table or GA flips, and only 1,365 carry any recorded review, so roughly 1,200 merged with no review on record. The rest leans on one fast approver: C15 approved 778 of his PRs, with no blocking review after 2026-08-04. Peers follow-up-fixed 31 PRs, 9 of them major. His own fail-closed change #86546 caused a two-hour fleet-wide credential outage, which he reversed in #122385, a self-repair chain. Most of the credentials-service work (#120995, #124844, #125029) merged near or after 2026-10-20, so it has no quality signal yet, and the 21-product migration shows merged call sites, not rollout. The team columns are mid-pack: requested_by 8 (P62), 269 approvals against 1 changes-requested. Even so, ~119 major episodes remain after the template discount, 3.2x the next candidate, so this does not unseat him.
replacement_reason: C17 has the cleaner per-PR record (quality_rate 0.993, P90, vs 0.986; 1 peer follow-up fix vs 31) and the strongest explicit review demand in the pool (requested_by 20, P100, vs 8), on billing and privacy majors such as #86160, #101932 and #101472.
rebuttal: Kept without a re-test: the objection rates itself weak. His 130 major+ episodes are 3.5x the next candidate (37), and about 119 remain after removing roughly 864 templated catalogue PRs. Both independent decisions ranked him #1. The templated share and the AI-only approval share (101 of 211 major PRs) are disclosed as caveats.

objection: His rank leans on network centrality and internal tooling. trust_rank P100 measures approval-network centrality, not being the most trusted approver, and much of it comes from a closed devex loop: C12 or C22 reviewed 261 of his 341 reviewed PRs, and 64% were seen by nobody else. Another 218 of 559 PRs have no recorded human review, which fits bot approval through Stamphog, a tool he owns (not verified). By audit note 6, his 0.997 first-pass rate is therefore not comparable with other candidates'. 176 PRs went to internal AI review tools (ws2-ws4) with only 6 majors and 5 deep reads. Deep-read Q averages 1.5, with Q=1 on the granian pin #104208 and the migration squash #91646, and 61% of diffs were truncated. The platform-wide 1000-row API cap #126411 (Q=1) merged after 2026-10-20 and has no quality signal yet. None of his work is landmark tier. He has 31 major episodes, fewer than C18 (37), C01 and C05 (32).
replacement_reason: C16 is nearly level on the core columns (28 vs 31 major episodes, quality_rate 0.980 vs 0.983) and has more explicit review demand (requested_by 15 vs 11), but his majors are customer-facing data correctness: the flag_evaluations migration across ingestion, HogQL, deletion and CDP (#124397, #117395, #110254) and CDP event-loss fixes (#121819), not internal developer tooling.
rebuttal: Tested: C07 beat the proposed replacement C16 (haacked) in both presentation orders (delivery 1,106 vs 697; shared mechanisms such as the common webhook transport used by many teams). trust_rank is shown with its literal meaning (approval-network centrality), and the closed review loop on his own PRs is disclosed. Both decisions ranked him #2.

replacement_reason: C08 matches him on major episodes (21 vs 20) with a better quality and review record (quality_rate 0.967 vs 0.952, first_pass_rate 1.0 vs 0.979, changes_requested 0.007 vs 0.029).
